# Wordsworth Writing

> Wordsworth Writing (wordsworthwriting.net) is an independent reference site with practical guides to technical writing, editing, document formatting in Microsoft Word, and U.S. government forms used by architecture/engineering/environmental (A/E/C) firms. All content is original; the site is not affiliated with the editing business previously operated at this domain.

## Guides

- [The SF330, explained](https://wordsworthwriting.net/sf330-form-in-microsoft-word/): Standard Form 330 (Architect-Engineer Qualifications) — how Parts I and II are organized, section-by-section notes, and how to manage the form in Microsoft Word.
- [The law behind the SF330](https://wordsworthwriting.net/sf330-requirements-brooks-act/): the Brooks Act's qualifications-based selection, the FAR Subpart 36.6 evaluation process, and the GAO/COFC protest decisions on common SF330 compliance mistakes.
- [Templates in Microsoft Word](https://wordsworthwriting.net/templates-in-microsoft-word/): building report, proposal, and resume templates on named styles; the template library an A/E/C firm needs.
- [Technical editing and document formatting](https://wordsworthwriting.net/technical-editing-document-formatting-services/): the levels of edit (proofreading, copyediting, line editing, structural editing), how editors price work, and what to ask before hiring one.
- [Writing tips](https://wordsworthwriting.net/writing-tips/): short usage notes — acronyms, numbers, hyphenation, common usage calls, style guides.
- [Structured settlement documents, explained](https://wordsworthwriting.net/structured-settlement-documents/): the settlement agreement, qualified assignment, annuity contract, and the disclosure/petition/court-order stack that governs transfers of payment rights.

## Optional

- [About this site](https://wordsworthwriting.net/about/): the history of the domain and the independence disclosure.
